text:
Fairfax County Public Schools announces updates for 2026-27 school year
L. P. James
Fairfax County Public Schools outlined on Aug. 4 several changes and reminders for families as they prepare for the 2026-27 school year, which begins Monday, August 24.
The district highlighted new policies, registration information, and important dates. Families are encouraged to register new students as soon as possible to participate in upcoming playdates, screenings, teacher visits, and open houses. The district also reminded parents to update their contact information and ensure that student immunizations are current; immunizations are required for all students attending public schools in Virginia.
FCPS will provide a list of upcoming immunization events in partnership with Inspire Health Alliance at designated locations throughout the school year. Additional resources are available through the Fairfax County Health Department clinics and Inova Cares Back-to-School Pediatric Health Fairs for eligible families. After receiving immunizations, parents should submit updated records to their child’s school or via SIS ParentVUE.
For transportation safety improvements this fall, FCPS will introduce a new student ID system for bus riders. Students who ride the bus will receive IDs that must be tapped when boarding or leaving the bus. The system is designed to ensure students use the correct buses and stops; it does not track student movement beyond these points. There is potential for future expansion of ID card uses.
Other announcements include updates to Student Rights and Responsibilities documents featuring Universal Grade Matrices by grade level; details about early release Wednesdays starting in late September at elementary schools; back-to-school night schedules by region; and an invitation for community feedback on a new School Resource Officer Memorandum of Understanding being developed with Fairfax County Police Department.
The district also noted key calendar dates such as Virginia’s sales tax holiday from August 7-9, and emphasized staying informed through weekly emails during the academic year.
summary: Families are encouraged to register new students as soon as possible to participate in upcoming playdates, screenings, teacher visits, and open houses. FCPS will provide a list of upcoming immunization events in partnership with Inspire Health Alliance at designated locations throughout the school year. For transportation safety improvements this fall, FCPS will introduce a new student ID system for bus riders.
